npcs.name: Magda Black
npcs.description: Magda Black is an Orc Operator boss who treats raiding like finance with better knives. In Cyr'ethael, she helps the Nefaric Veil turn tribute, fear, protection rackets, and luxury theft into a polished business model, preferring clean profit over messy slaughter. She is elegant, calculating, and cruel in the way of someone who thinks mercy is acceptable only when it earns interest.
npcs.settlementAndAncestryTexture: Cyr'ethael is a Town in Iazethas, under Triumvirate, with low danger, Beach and grass with water, Farming, Partial forest terrain. Local records favor Altruistic, Lawful, Cooperative, Honorable civic habits; common communities include Human, Halfling — Lightfoot Halfling, Halfling — Stout Halfling, Kender, Kithkin. Orc reads through the Human entry of the race compendium, within Humans, Near-Humans, and Mixed Heritage, marked by Nebyrr. The local form is read through Half-Orc (Human + Orc Lineage). Humans are highly adaptable and found in nearly every environment across the world. They are known for their cultural diversity, short generational cycles, and unmatched versatility among mortal races. Table cues: Resourceful, Skillful, Versatile; starting tendency Neutral - Neutral - Neutral - Neutral.
rumors: Magda Black knows why an ichor ledger changed hands last Valkhaday.
Magda Black has a contact in Vorathûn who will deny everything.
plotHooks: Magda Black asks the party to protect a household member without revealing why.
A rival faction offers proof that Magda Black's public story is incomplete.

npcs.name: Piera Wrightquill
npcs.description:
Piera Wrightquill is a relentless lunar elf reporter with a talent for turning rumor, ledgers, overheard threats, and inconvenient witnesses into public scandal. Her moonlit elven instincts make her curious, adaptable, and difficult to intimidate, while Sigrananna’s influence gives her a sharp hunter’s patience when stalking a corrupt official through paper trails instead of forests.
In Cyr'ethael, a town in dragon-ruled Iazethas, Piera’s broadsheets regularly challenge draconic law, civic silence, price-fixing, poisoned canals, militia corruption, and anyone powerful enough to think truth should stay buried. She is sarcastic, lonely, brave to the point of recklessness, and deeply protective of her household, using the Public Broadsheet Office and the Brass Concordat to expose rot before it becomes accepted law.
